summary.text: An 18-year-old man underwent a gross total resection of a sporadic vestibular schwannoma via a retrosigmoid approach in the authors department, then a classic hypoglossal-facial neurorrhaphy, after which facial nerve function improved to House-Brackmann grade IV.

Eight years later a recurrent tumor with a maximal size of 33 mm was diagnosed, which had progressed toward the petrous apex. Revision surgery via a middle fossa approach achieved total resection and the postoperative course was uneventful; no tumor regrowth was noted over 11 years of follow-up.

summary.text: A 54-year-old woman presented with facial nerve paresis one year after a subtotal vestibular schwannoma resection in another center. Admission examination revealed deafness, right-sided dysmmetry, dizziness, subjective diplopia, right facial hypoaesthesia and soft palate paresis, without difficulty swallowing, and follow-up MRI showed a tumor remnant in the right CPA, intrameatally. Coronal and axial MR images at one year after the initial surgery show growth after stereotactic radiosurgery (stated in the figure caption only).

Revision surgery via a retrosigmoid approach with facial neurorrhaphy was performed. Hypoglossal paresis developed after revision surgery and subsequently resolved; two months later otorrhea with chronic otitis media developed, CT showed a fistula between the CPA, mastoid air cells and external acoustic canal, and the patient underwent petrosectomy. The subsequent postoperative course was uneventful and follow-up MRI confirmed the completeness of the resection.

MR images and a photograph 11 months after revision surgery show the results of a gross total resection with satisfactory facial nerve function. At 2-year follow-up, facial nerve function improved to House-Brackmann grade III.

summary.text: A 53-year-old man presented with right facial and abducens nerve paresis and right-sided deafness after a partial vestibular schwannoma removal 6 months earlier in another center; a tumor remnant was located close to the porus acusticus.

Revision surgery via a translabyrinthine approach was performed. The postoperative course was uneventful and he was discharged one week after surgery. At 1-year follow-up facial nerve function improved to House-Brackmann grade III and a postoperative MRI revealed no tumor remnant. Photographs show no visible tongue atrophy and a straight tongue position.

article_limitations: The article reports 29 consecutive patients; only three are individually described (Illustrative Cases 1 to 3), so the roster is incomplete. All other results (Tables 1 to 4, results and discussion text) are cohort-level and are not copied to individual patients.
Source text is not explicit on which of the 29 patients the illustrative cases are in the cohort tables; no cohort statistic is attributed to a case.
Facial neurorrhaphy type (hemihypoglossal) is named as eligibility/plan for Cases 2 and 3 but not stated as performed in the segment text; the Case 2 caption states facial neurorrhaphy was performed.
Case 2 caption mentions stereotactic radiosurgery that the case text does not; timing and date are not stated.
Eight years in Case 1 is anchored to the preceding sentence only; no other dates are given for any case.
Caption-layer visual status not_inspected; actual 3 JPEGs inspected in the separate visual submission.
Supplement SM1 (Table_1.xlsx) is listed in the source; its contents are reviewed in the supplement manifest sidecar.

Cohort inconsistencies noted but not attributed to cases: abstract says HB grades II-IV for weakness while Methods give II-VI; complication rate is 13.8% in Results and 10.3% in Discussion with CSF leak rates swapped between sections; Table 4 percentages for HB IV, V and VI at long-term outcome are printed as 7.13.
Abstract states that 11 patients received HHFNs, while the Results state 12 (also 12/15 in Methods); not attributed to cases.
Section headings for Illustrative Cases 2 and 3 name a hemihypoglossal-facial neurorrhaphy, but the case sentences give it only as eligibility; the HHFN is not recorded as performed.
